items.titleZh: 梅赛德斯称缺乏资金升级2026赛车，难追迈凯伦开发步伐
items.summaryZh: 梅赛德斯表示因资金不足，无法通过紧急升级回应迈凯伦的强势复苏，难以跟上对手的开发速度。迈凯伦在匈牙利和荷兰大奖赛分两阶段引入的升级效果显著，兰多·诺里斯在荷兰大奖赛凭借节奏和更好的轮胎管理超越起步领先安东内利，取得赛季两连胜。
items.originalTitle: 梅赛德斯称“没钱”为2026年赛车升级，无法跟上迈凯伦开发步伐
items.summaryEn: Mercedes says it cannot respond to McLaren's F1 resurgence with an urgent upgrade because it hasn't got the money for extra developments. McLaren's two-stage upgrade across the Hungarian and Dutch Grands Prix proved decisive, as Lando Norris's pace and superior tyre management allowed him to overhaul early leader Kimi Antonelli and claim his second consecutive victory.
detailZh: 梅赛德斯表示，无法通过紧急升级来应对迈凯伦在F1中的强势复苏，因为他们没有“钱”在赛车上投入额外的研发。
上周日的荷兰大奖赛中，兰多·诺里斯为迈凯伦取得了本赛季连续第二场胜利，他的速度和更出色的轮胎管理让他得以超越比赛早期的领先者基米·安东内利。
迈凯伦在匈牙利和荷兰两站大奖赛分两阶段实施的重大升级所带来的跨越式进步令梅赛德斯感到意外，并让积分榜领跑者安东内利确信自己的车队已不再拥有最快的赛车。
在这种情况下，车队通常会加快升级的步伐，以帮助梅赛德斯重返领先位置。
然而，车队领队托托·沃尔夫表示，他的车队无法偏离自赛季开始以来所采用的分散部署研发的策略——因为在成本上限的限制下，他们没有余力引入太多升级。
“我们没有钱把研发成果装到赛车上，”他说。
“我以前就说过，我们正努力在整个赛季中均匀分配这些升级，根据我们的计算来判断何时能带来最大的升级，并优化锦标赛积分。我们做不到的事情就是做不到。”
自年初以来，梅赛德斯在研发支出方面一直比竞争对手保守得多。
自加拿大大奖赛以来，该车就没有进行过重大升级，并且在荷兰大奖赛上选择不加入其最接近的竞争对手的行列，不带来任何重要的新部件。
根据国际汽联（FIA）公布的2026年已申报升级项目的官方数据，就引进的升级数量而言，梅赛德斯远远落后。
法拉利引入了40个新部件，红牛和迈凯伦为38个，而梅赛德斯仅引入了24个。
然而，这些基本数字并不能完全反映在研发上花费了多少，因为例如一个新的底板，其成本要远高于一个后视镜罩。
一项加权分析对每个新部件给出成本评级，结果显示红牛在四大领先车队中位居榜首，略高于迈凯伦，法拉利第三，梅赛德斯则落后不少。
目前尚不清楚，为什么梅赛德斯在升级方面如此保守，却没有像其他车队那样拥有额外的研发支出空间。
一种猜测是，梅赛德斯较早地将更多资源投入2026年项目，希望先在积分榜上建立起足够大的优势，从而后期无需在研发上花费太多，同时让对手打消把钱浪费在一场他们无法夺冠的争斗中的念头。
但任何想凭借自身速度扩大优势、让对手无法染指总冠军的希望，都被赛季初的可靠性问题所打断，这些问题让法拉利、以及现在的迈凯伦一直保持在前列。
当The 比赛问及早期的开支是否解释了为什么梅赛德斯似乎不像带来更多升级的其他车队那样具备同等能力时，沃尔夫并不认同这种说法。
“我们在最初的研发阶段是否花费太多？我不这么认为，”他说。
“我只是觉得我们是一个拥有一定规模和基础设施的组织。而且，你知道，在这方面，我们当时有一辆非常快的车。
“由于可靠性问题，我们损失了大约50到100分，否则我们本可以比今天拥有更大的领先优势。
“除此之外，我们只是在继续执行原本的计划，以及财务现实对我们意味着什么。”
梅赛德斯副领队Bradley Lord在夏休期前表示，车队有大量研发潜力正在系统中推进——问题只是这些部件何时被带到赛道上。
“目前有相当可观的性能提升正在生产体系中推进，它们将从夏休结束后的比赛开始陆续应用到赛车上。”
迈凯伦并不认为梅赛德斯在成本上限方面处于被动，并认为对方在实际引进升级件方面拥有比其所暗示的更多自由度。
随着额外成本上限豁免（两笔各300万美元）被加入规则以帮助车队适应2027年及以后的新动力单元规则，这一点尤其正确。
当The 比赛问及沃尔夫关于车队在支出上处于被动局面的言论时，迈凯伦车队领队安德烈亚·斯特拉表示：“我愿意相信你，但实际上我并不相信。我不相信，因为得益于2027年动力单元规则，所有车队在成本上限申报中都将获得一笔额外额度。”
“我确信梅赛德斯在看到对手们有点提升水平之后，现在一定会兑现他们的研发成果。可以肯定的是，这正在实际发生。”
“我确信他们在风洞里的赛车要比现在赛道上的那辆快不少，他们会希望把其中一些潜力转化为应用到真实赛车上的升级。我非常肯定他们会有升级。当然，如果没有那会很好，但我甚至不愿意去想那种情况。”
沃尔夫认为，最终梅赛德斯的成本上限策略只能通过整个赛季来评判——因为可能存在其他车队在赛季后期不得不削减开支，而他的车队还有更多余量的情况。
“你会看到，到了赛季末，他们是否还能像现在这样往赛车上部署那么多部件，”他说。
“也许有人的策略不同，在年初和年中投入更多，而到赛季末投入较少。”
今年早些时候，沃尔夫曾暗示梅赛德斯无法理解马拉内罗车队（法拉利）怎么能为SF-26带来这么多激进的升级，这惹恼了法拉利。
沃尔夫的立场引发了法拉利车队领队弗雷德·瓦塞尔（Fred Vasseur）的尖锐回应。
"我觉得托托和梅赛德斯说这话相当讽刺," 他说。"但红牛在研发或者梅赛德斯在研发的时候，他们就是天才。轮到我们研发的时候，我们就是在作弊。"
让梅赛德斯在选择何时投入升级的问题上更加复杂的是，安东内利将在他的主场意大利大奖赛接受引擎处罚——因此他在那里争夺胜利的机会将受到阻碍。
沃尔夫补充道："从理论上讲，我们的计算表明那是搭载新引擎的最佳赛道。"
“显然，算法不会把国籍考虑在内。但我们来这里是为了争夺冠军，而不是为了获得最多的公关曝光。所以，是的，这就是我们要做的。至于George，如果我们决定采取这个方案，相关的讨论还在进行中。”
detailEn: Mercedes says it can't respond to McLaren’s Formula 1 resurgence with an urgent upgrade because it hasn’t “got the money” to put extra developments on its car.

Lando Norris delivered his second consecutive victory of the season for McLaren in the Dutch Grand Prix on Sunday as his pace and better tyre management allowed him to overhaul early race leader Kimi Antonelli.

The major step that a two-stage upgrade from McLaren over the Hungarian and Dutch Grands Prix unleashed has caught Mercedes by surprise – and left championship leader Antonelli convinced his squad no longer has the fastest car.
Such a scenario would typically trigger a move to fast-track upgrades to help get Mercedes back to the front.

However, team boss Toto Wolff has suggested that his outfit cannot divert from the strategy it has employed since the start of the campaign to spread out its developments – as it does not have the leeway under the cost cap to bring many changes through.
“We haven't got the money to put developments on the car,” he said.

“I said it before, we are trying to evenly split that through the season, based on our calculations of when we can bring the biggest updates and optimising the championship points. We just can't do what we can't do.”
Mercedes has been much less aggressive than its rivals since the start of the year with its development spending.
It has not had a major upgrade since the Canadian Grand Prix and elected against joining its closest rivals in bringing any major new parts to the Dutch Grand Prix.
Based on the official FIA figures for declared upgrades over 2026, Mercedes is well behind when it comes to the number it has brought.
Ferrari has introduced 40 new components, Red Bull and McLaren 38, while Mercedes has introduced just 24.
However, those basic numbers do not tell the full story of how much spending has been done on development, as a new floor, for example, costs a lot more than a mirror shroud.
A weighted analysis giving a cost grade for each new component puts Red Bull at the top of the leading four teams, just ahead of McLaren, with Ferrari third and Mercedes quite a bit adrift.
It is not clear why, after being so conservative with its upgrades, Mercedes does not have the same headroom as other teams for extra development spending.

One theory could be that it invested more into the 2026 project early on in the hope of building up such an advantage in the championship that it did not need to spend much on development later on and rivals were put off wasting money on a title they could not win.
But any hopes of capitalising on its pace and putting the championship out of reach of its rivals were derailed by early-season reliability woes that have kept Ferrari, and now McLaren, in touch.
When asked by The Race about whether early spending explained why Mercedes did not appear to have the same capabilities as other teams who have brought more, Wolff was not convinced.
“Did we spend too much at the beginning in the initial development? I don't think so,” he said.
“I just think we're an organisation that has a certain size and infrastructure. And, you know, in that respect, we had a really quick car.
“We left between 50 and 100 points on the table with reliability issues and that would have given us a little bit more of a gap than we have today.
“Other than that, we're just continuing to execute what the plan was and what the financial realities mean for us.”

Speaking before the summer break, Mercedes deputy team principal Bradley Lord said that the squad had plenty of development potential coming through the system – it was just a question of when items were brought to the track.
“There's a decent amount of performance working its way through the production machinery at the moment, that will start coming to the car from the races after shutdown.”
McLaren is not convinced that Mercedes is on the back foot when it comes to cost cap limits, and thinks it has more freedom to bring upgrades than it is suggesting.

This is especially true with an extra cost cap allowance, of two lots of $3 million, that has been added to the regulations aimed at helping teams adjust to the new power unit rules for 2027 and beyond.

Asked by The Race about Wolff’s remarks suggesting it was on the backfoot with spending, McLaren team principal Andrea Stella said: “I would like to believe you, but I actually don't believe you. I don't believe it, because thanks to the 2027 power unit regulations, all teams will have an allowance in their reporting for the cost-cap.
“I'm sure that Mercedes, having seen that the rivals are kind of elevating the game, I'm sure they will now cash in on their development. Surely, it's happening on the ground.

“I'm sure the car in the windtunnel is quite a bit faster than the car they have on track, and they will want to now convert some of this potential into upgrades that make it to the real car. I'm pretty sure that they will have upgrades. Obviously, it would be good if not, but I don't even want to think it.”

Wolff thinks that ultimately the Mercedes cost cap strategy can only be judged over the full season – as it could be that others may have to switch off spending later in the campaign while his outfit has some more headroom.
“You will see how towards the end of the season if they're going to be able to deploy as much stuff onto the car as they do now,” he said.
“Someone might have a different strategy in spending more at the beginning and in the middle of the year than towards the end.”
Earlier in the year, Wolff annoyed Ferrari by suggesting Mercedes could not understand how the Maranello squad had been able to be so aggressive with bringing upgrades to the SF-26.
Wolff’s stance triggered a pointed response from Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur.
"I found it quite ironic coming from Toto and Mercedes," he said. "But when Red Bull is developing or when Mercedes is developing, they are genius. When we are developing, we are cheating.”

Adding to Mercedes’ complications over the choice of timing of committing to bring an upgrade is that Antonelli will take an engine penalty at his home Italian Grand Prix – so his chances of fighting for the win there will be hampered.
Wolff added: “In theory, our calculations say that that's the best track to take it.

“Obviously, algorithms don't take the nationality into consideration. But we're here to fight for a championship and not get the most PR. So, yeah, that's what we're going to do. With George, the discussions are ongoing on if we were to take it.”

items.originalTitle: F1荷兰大奖赛混乱中的赢家与输家
items.summaryEn: After a dull sprint on Saturday raised fears of an anticlimactic Dutch Grand Prix, a sudden shower one hour before Sunday's race caused enough chaos at Zandvoort to add drama. Although the rain did not persist into the race, it made the track slippery and led to carnage at the end of lap 1.
detailZh: F1混乱的荷兰大奖赛：赢家与输家
F1荷兰大奖赛以轰动的方式落幕，成为近年来最精彩纷呈的比赛之一，诞生了多位引人注目的赢家和输家
如果在周六那场令人昏昏欲睡的冲刺赛之后，还有人担心荷兰会以一场无聊的比赛为自己的F1复兴之旅送别，那么这种担心在周日正赛开始前一小时的一场突然降雨中被一扫而空，当时发车区刚开始向观众开放
雨没有持续到正赛期间，但恰好造成了足够的混乱，使赞德沃特的沙丘赛道变得湿滑，导致第一圈结束时发生了多车相撞的混乱局面
在所有人当中，偏偏是本土英雄维斯塔潘在这种条件下栽了跟头，他犯了一个罕见的错误，在驶入主直道时右脚踩得太急。本应全油门通过的Luyendyk弯特别湿滑，Verstappen在内侧压到白线后直接滑向了外侧护墙。
最终的结果是一场严重撞车，不过这位荷兰车手幸运地没有被随后驶来的车流撞上。在这项赛事的告别之战上，这不是他或大批身穿橙色服装的车迷所期望的结局，但这位四届世界冠军和赞德沃特赛道都曾有过一段美好时光——Verstappen赢得了前三次比赛的胜利。Verstappen的续约合同——据称将让他在F1留到2030年——也应该能缓解这次失利的打击。
周六的冲刺赛并没有让迈凯伦有多少信心，车队在比赛节奏和中性胎管理上的劣势使其无法跟上冠军拉塞尔，而法拉利看起来也明显更快。
但到了周日，在Norris的手中，搭载升级套件的迈凯伦就是另一番景象了。虽然Norris未能在静止重新起步时挡住Antonelli，但在倍耐力硬胎上，这位卫冕世界冠军简直是势不可挡，他超越了当时的领跑者，并在同一圈又超掉了汉密尔顿。
他的车队领队安德里亚·斯特拉将好成绩归功于车队在冲刺赛表现糟糕得多之后对赛车调校所做的调整，但同时也特别称赞了诺里斯，因为奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里在另一辆车上挣扎得要多得多。
"我认为兰多在理解如何使用这种（硬胎）配方方面多了一挡，"斯特拉说。"在这样的条件下，我想这正是他能够展现自己天然驾驶风格的地方。"
正如他最近在布达佩斯和赞德沃特的大奖赛胜利所表明的那样，诺里斯可以说正处于他的巅峰状态。
不同的赛车，不同的角色，不同的车队领导层。利亚姆·劳森这次重返红牛的一次性机会，与他2025年初在那支车队灾难性的首秀相比，所处的环境可谓天壤之别——那次经历仅仅持续了两站比赛。
任何与他共事过或曾经共事过的人交谈，都能明显看出Lawson也发生了变化——这段磨炼性格的经历让他更加成熟，作为一名大奖赛车手也更加全面。
说出来容易，但在荷兰站，Lawson实际上得到了一个意想不到的机会，用事实来证明这一点。他顶替受伤的哈贾尔出赛，在这一场临时代打的周末中镇定自若地坚持了下来，尽管除了动力单元之外，他所驾驶的这辆赛车对他来说“完全是不同的”。
周日能拿到的只有遥远的第一名开外的第七位，因为红牛车队以不小的差距排在速度第四快的车队之列。这就是红牛对替补车手所能要求的全部。
又一个周末过去了，法拉利拥有一辆很快的赛车，却不知怎的没能把它带上领奖台。从排位赛中不太理想的车迷圈计时圈，到进站，再到比赛策略，比赛周末的执行依然是这支车队（Scuderia）的痛点。
刘易斯·汉密尔顿（汉密尔顿）在周日做出了一个敏锐的观察，此前他对法拉利在是否与夏尔·勒克莱尔（勒克莱尔）交换位置或让队友进站这一决定上磨磨蹭蹭感到厌烦，最终法拉利选择了让队友进站。当乔治·拉塞尔（拉塞尔）被要求与基米·安东内利（安东内利）交换位置时，这位英国车手并不太情愿，但还是立即执行了，两位车手在过程中都没有损失太多时间。
“梅赛德斯就是这样执行的，”汉密尔顿说。“他们有车在领跑，正在争夺总冠军，他们立刻就做了。而在这里，我只能坐在后面干等，损失了好几秒。有些事情我们需要私下里讨论。”
如果没有最后阶段的虚拟安全车，情况本可能有所不同——虚拟安全车很可能帮助拉塞尔守住了领奖台位置，免受汉密尔顿的威胁。但随着这位七届世界冠军和法拉利试图凭借动力不足的引擎继续参与争夺，所有这些小问题正开始不断累积。
在周五，由于本田升级版引擎的驾驶性问题，费尔南多·阿隆索（阿隆索）和队友兰斯·斯特罗尔（斯特罗尔）连留在赛道上都很困难，更不用说延续车队在匈牙利站的进步了，赞德福特周末对阿斯顿·马丁来说原本前景相当黯淡。
周日的比赛依然没有出现奇迹，但AMR26赛车的表现足以让阿隆索大胆的一停策略奏效，压过了阿尔派的加斯利和小红牛的两名车手。
“F1不是一项神秘的运动，”阿隆索说，他是自1974年以来首位45岁及以上还能拿分的车手。“你必须带来性能并超越竞争对手才能拿分，而我们正在做的就是这个。所以，祝贺银石站的每一个人，希望我们能带来更多。”
你可以大做文章地谈论塞恩斯与阿尔本在比赛结束时的碰撞。但比这场威廉姆斯内斗本身更糟糕的是，这次碰撞——由塞恩斯的旧硬胎在1号弯锁死引发——完全没有意义，因为这两位车手争的只是他们自己之间的第15名。
在进展不足的赛车套件在阿塞拜疆获得急需的升级之前，威廉姆斯将处于挣扎求生的状态。但在阿斯顿·马丁取得重大进步之后，威廉姆斯现在只能和凯迪拉克竞争，状态好的时候还能和哈斯争一争。
本周的好消息是，两位车手都已承诺明年继续留队，这消除了近几周来笼罩着车队的种种噪音和干扰。但正如车队领队James Vowles周五承认的那样，威廉姆斯不会有任何短期解决办法。
正如劳森在成功重返红牛后完成了圆满轮回、值得称赞一样，YukI Tsunoda也同样值得称赞。这位日本车手在2026年整年坐冷板凳后，在一次临时出场中表现抢眼，他全身心投入其中，细细品味着这段他原本不确定还能否再次拥有的经历。
通过角田裕毅与Honda精心培养的关系，IndyCar的未来或许正在等待着他。但在上个周末，这位26岁的车手可以再次称自己为F1车手，而且他整周末都紧紧咬住正式车手Arvid Lindblad，做得相当不错。
"说实话，我很怀念这种感觉，追逐那最后几毫秒的感觉，"Tsunoda在排位赛后说，"我非常享受。"
在周日刚刚与积分失之交臂后，他补充道：“我知道自己能做到什么，而且我认为我基本上已经向围场里的大多数人展示了我能做到什么。
“现在就看我的经纪人以及其他还没有决定明年车手阵容的车队了，看他们想不想要我。请给我打电话吧！”Tsunoda 开玩笑说完后便被匆匆带走了。
你怎么能不为 霍肯伯格 欢呼呢？他在第 1 圈结束时凭借出色的反应能力，救了他的 奥迪 队友 博托莱托，使其免于一场可怕的事故？你不能不，所以为他的表现点赞。
detailEn: Winners and losers from F1's chaotic Dutch Grand Prix
Formula 1's Dutch Grand Prix went out with a bang, producing one of the more eventful editions in recent memory which yielded several high-profile winners and losers

If there were any fears after Saturday's mind-numbing sprint display that the Netherlands would send off its Formula 1 revival with a dud, then those fears were washed away in a sudden shower one hour before Sunday's race, around the time the starting grid started opening for business.
The rain didn't persist into the race itself, but caused just enough havoc to make Zandvoort's dune loop slippery, leading to carnage at the end of lap 1.

Of all people, it was home hero Max Verstappen who tripped up in the conditions, making a rare mistake by being too eager with his right foot coming onto the main straight. The otherwise flat-out Luyendyk corner was particularly damp, with Verstappen veering straight into the outside wall after tapping the white line on the inside.

The end result was a huge crash, though the Dutchman was fortunate not to be collected by oncoming traffic. It's not the end result he or the army of orange clad fans were hoping for on the event's swansong, but both the four-time world champion and Zandvoort have had a good run, with Verstappen winning the first three editions. Verstappen's contract extension, which is supposed to keep him in F1 until 2030, should soften the blow too.

Saturday's sprint didn't particularly fill McLaren with confidence, with the team's inferior race pace and tyre management on the medium compound making it unable to keep up with winner George Russell, while Ferrari also looked intrinsically quicker.

But in the hands of Norris, Sunday was a different story for the upgraded McLaren. While Norris was unable to hold off Antonelli on the standing restart, on Pirelli's hard tyre the reigning world champion was an absolute demon as he swept past the erstwhile leader and then picked off Lewis Hamilton on the same lap.
His team boss Andrea Stella credited the team's set-up adjustments after a much poorer sprint, but also reserved special praise for Norris as Oscar Piastri struggled much more aboard the other car.
"I think Lando had an extra [gear] in terms of understanding how to use this [hard] compound," Stella said. "These conditions, I think this is where he can express his natural driving style."
As his most recent grand prix wins in Budapest and Zandvoort have shown, Norris is arguably operating at his peak right now.

Different car, different role, different team leadership. The circumstances around Liam Lawson's one-off Red Bull return couldn't have been more different than his first calamitous adventure with the squad at the start of 2025, which lasted all of two rounds.
Speak to anyone who works or has worked with him, and it is clear Lawson has changed too - more mature for the character-building experience, and more well-rounded as a grand prix driver.

That's all very easy to say, but in the Netherlands Lawson was actually handed a surprise opportunity to back that up with facts. Subbing for the injured Isack Hadjar, he soldiered on through his one-off weekend with aplomb, despite driving what he experienced as an "entirely different" car other than the power unit.
A distant seventh-place was all that was on offer on Sunday as Red Bull was the fourth-fastest team by some distance. This is all Red Bull could have asked for from its stand-in.

Yet another weekend goes by where Ferrari has a quick car but somehow manages not to bring it to the podium. Race weekend execution remains a sore topic for the Scuderia, between sub-optimal out-laps in qualifying to pitstops to race strategy.

Lewis Hamilton made an astute observation on Sunday, after getting fed up with Ferrari dilly-dallying on its decision to either swap positions with Charles Leclerc or pit his team-mate, as ended up happening. When George Russell was asked to swap with Kimi Antonelli, the Briton didn't particularly like it but immediately acted, with neither driver losing much time in the process.

"Mercedes execute like that," Hamilton said. "They've got the car that's fighting for the championship in the lead, and they did it straight away. Here I'm sitting back, losing seconds. Something that we need to discuss offline."

Things could have been different without the late virtual safety car, which likely saved Russell's podium spot from Hamilton. But all those little things are starting to add up as the seven-time world champion and Ferrari are trying to stay in the fight with an under-powered engine.

The Zandvoort weekend was shaping up to be quite bleak for Aston Martin on Friday when driveability issues with Honda's upgraded engine made it hard enough for Fernando Alonso and team-mate Lance Stroll to stay on the black stuff, never mind build on the team's Hungary progress.

There still weren't any miracles on Sunday, but there was enough performance in the AMR26 to make a bold one-stop strategy work for Alonso, getting one over Alpine's Pierre Gasly and the Racing Bulls drivers.

"Formula 1 is not a mysterious sport," said Alonso, the first driver aged 45 or older to score points since 1974. "You have to bring performance and outperform competitors to score points and it's what we are doing. So, congratulations everyone in Silverstone and hopefully we can bring more."

You could make a big deal about the contact between Carlos Sainz and Alex Albon at the end of the race. But much more damning than the Williams-on-Williams violence itself is the fact that the collision, triggered by Sainz locking up his old hard tyres in Turn 1, was utterly meaningless, as the two drivers were racing nobody but themselves for 15th.

Williams is stuck in survival mode until its underdeveloped package receives some much-needed upgrades in Azerbaijan. But following Aston Martin's significant step forward, it's now just racing Cadillac and - on a good day - Haas.

The good news of this week is that both drivers have committed their future to the team for next year, removing some of the noise and distractions that were clouding the picture in recent weeks. But, as team principal James Vowles admitted on Friday, there won't be any short-term fixes for Williams.

As Liam Lawson deserves praise for coming full circle on his successful Red Bull return, so does YukI Tsunoda. The Japanese driver was a spark plug on his one-off outing after spending 2026 on the sidelines, soaking it all in as he savoured an experience he wasn't sure he would ever be granted again.

A future in IndyCar may well await, through Yuki Tsunoda's carefully cultivated Honda connections. But last weekend, the 26-year-old could call himself an F1 driver again, and he did a decent job sticking close to regular driver Arvid Lindblad throughout the weekend.
"Honestly, I missed this kind of feeling, chasing those last few milliseconds," Tsunoda said after qualifying. "I am super enjoying it."
After just missing out on a point on Sunday, he added: "I know what I can do and I think I pretty much showed what I can do to most of the paddock.
"Now it's up to my manager and other teams, who haven't decided yet about next year's line-up, if they want to have me or not. Call me, please!" Tsunoda joked before being whisked away.
How can you not give Nico Hulkenberg a shout-out for his outstanding reflexes at the end of lap 1, which saved his Audi team-mate Gabriel Bortoleto from an awful accident? You can't, so fair play.

items.summaryZh: 乔治·拉塞尔表示，让队友兼冠军竞争对手安东内利超过自己是正确的决定，这符合他的比赛利益。

items.originalTitle: 拉塞尔为让安东内利升至第二的“公平”决定辩护
items.summaryEn: George Russell said letting his team mate and championship rival overtake him was the correct decision which minimised the risk to their races.
detailZh: 乔治·拉塞尔表示，让队友兼冠军竞争对手超过自己是正确的决定，这将对两人比赛的风险降到了最低。
安德烈亚·基米·安东内利在晚段虚拟安全车期间多进一次站之前一直领先拉塞尔。当安东内利随后追近拉塞尔时，梅赛德斯下令两人交换位置。
拉塞尔服从了指令，尽管这让安东内利在两人之间的冠军争夺中净赚六分。这抵消了拉塞尔在前一天冲刺赛中取得的收获。
然而拉塞尔表示，让队友超过对梅赛德斯而言是正确的做法。
“我们一直说，作为一支车队，当我们采用不同策略时，我们绝不互相争斗，总是会交换位置，这一直是我们的规则，”他解释道。
“事实是，基米在虚拟安全车之前领先我，他尝试了不同的做法来保护我们车队。他基本上复制了法拉利的做法。”
尽管拉塞尔认为他有机会成功守住位置不让安东内利超过——正如他后来对刘易斯·汉密尔顿所做的那样，部分得益于另一次虚拟安全车时段的时机——但他也表示，试图防守可能会危及自己的比赛。
“我能把他挡在身后吗？也许吧。但同样也可能变成第五名。所以最终，你知道，他配得上第二名。我认为第三名对我来说是公平的结果。”
拉塞尔在比赛开始时落后于安东内利，随后被困在奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里身后，始终未能追回与队友的差距。“很艰难，”他说。
“第一次虚拟安全车出现的时机对我来说相当尴尬，因为我觉得硬胎上非常强。我认为基米和我的比赛有点相反。我中性胎阶段很艰难，他中性胎阶段非常强，然后我硬胎阶段很强，他则很挣扎。
“但那次虚拟安全车给了刘易斯一次免费进站，显然基米也进站了。从那时起，我知道自己会受到威胁。
“我在高速弯中管理得足够好，让我在第三赛段能够快速，并在进入一号弯（塔赞弯）时防守。所以我对那表现感到满意。”
detailEn: George Russell said letting his team mate and championship rival overtake him was the correct decision which minimised the risk to their races.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli ran ahead of Russell until he made an extra pit stop during a late Virtual Safety Car period. When Antonelli closed on Russell afterwards, Mercedes ordered the pair to swap positions.
Russell complied, though it handed Antonelli a six-point swing in the championship fight between the pair of them. That erased the gain Russell made in the previous day’s sprint race.
However Russell said letting his team mate by was the correct thing to do for Mercedes.
“We’ve always said as a team, when we’re on different strategies, we’re never going to fight and we’re always going to invert, and that’s always just been our rules,” he explained.
“The fact is Kimi was ahead of me before the VSC and he tried something different to protect us as a team. He kind of copy-pasted what the Ferraris did.”

Although Russell believes there was a chance he could have successfully defended his position from Antonelli – as he later did with Lewis Hamilton, thanks partly to the timing of another VSC period – he also said trying to defend could have compromised his race.
“Could I have kept him behind? Maybe. But equally it could have been a P5 as well. So, in the end, you know, he deserved to be P2. I think P3 was a fair result for me.”
Russell fell behind Antonelli at the start of the race, then got stuck behind Oscar Piastri and never managed to get back on terms with his team mate. “It was tough,” he said.

“The first VSC came at a pretty awkward timing for me because I felt really strong on the hard [tyre]. I think Kimi’s and my race was kind of the opposite. I had a tough medium stint, he had a very strong medium stint, then I had a strong hard stint, he was struggling.
“But that VSC gave Lewis a free pit stop and obviously Kimi pitted as well. And from there on in, I knew I was going to be under threat.
“I was managing enough in the high-speed corners to allow me to be fast in sector three and defending into turn one [Tarzan]. So I was pleased with that performance.”
keyPointsZh: 安东内利在晚段虚拟安全车期间多进一次站，随后梅赛德斯下令两人交换位置。
这次让车使安东内利在两人冠军争夺中净赚六分，抵消了拉塞尔前一天冲刺赛的收获。
拉塞尔称车队规则是不同策略下从不互相争斗、总是交换位置，并认为第三名对自己是公平结果。
keyPointsEn: Antonelli made an extra pit stop during a late Virtual Safety Car period, after which Mercedes ordered the pair to swap positions.
The swap handed Antonelli a six-point swing in the championship fight, erasing Russell's gain from the previous day's sprint race.
Russell said the team's rule is never to fight on different strategies and always to invert, and called third place a fair result for himself.

items.summaryZh: 安东内利表示，荷兰大奖赛上他的额外进站可能并非正确决定，这一策略也让队友拉塞尔面临风险。

items.originalTitle: 安东内利称额外进站“也让乔治面临风险” | 一级方程式
items.summaryEn: Antonelli said his extra pit stop at the Dutch Grand Prix may not have been the right decision, and that the strategy also put his team mate Russell at risk.
detailZh: 安德烈亚·基米·安东内利并不确信自己在荷兰大奖赛上的额外进站是正确的决定，因为这有可能危及他的比赛。
这位梅赛德斯车手在比赛还剩16圈时额外进站，利用了比赛末段的虚拟安全车时段。这让他从第二位掉到第三位，位于队友乔治·拉塞尔之后。
在梅赛德斯命令拉塞尔让车后，安东内利得以重新超越队友回到第二位。然而安东内利未能追近领先的兰多·诺里斯。
赛后安东内利表示，这一策略决定不必要地让两人的比赛都面临风险，尽管他此前一套轮胎确实跑得很挣扎。
“对我来说下半场很艰难，尤其是最后一段用硬胎的时候，”他说。“我真的很挣扎。我对赛车缺乏信心，这并不容易。”
“然后显然我们在虚拟安全车下进站了，那也有点棘手。但后来乔治也是，我得感谢他，因为他让我的处境轻松了很多。”
“但我仍然认为，我们或许本可以留在外面，用同一套轮胎一直跑到最后，因为那让我们有点冒险。而且，我觉得我们也让乔治面临风险，因为他不得不让我过去等等。”
尽管他领跑了比赛的大部分时间，安东内利表示他不太可能赢得比赛。“我仍然认为，归根结底，就当时的情况而言，车队的执行非常出色，”他说。“我认为今天（第二名）已经是我们能做到的极限了，因为迈凯伦的速度，尤其是下半场，实在太强了。”
“这对我来说是一个艰难周末的不错收尾，我一直在与赛车的感觉作斗争，自己犯了很多错误——冲刺排位赛、排位赛，还有今天正赛对兰多，我本可以防守得更好一些，”他补充道。“所以这个周末肯定有我没做好的地方，而且感觉肯定也没有那么好。”
detailEn: Andrea Kimi Antonelli was not convinced his extra pit stop in the Dutch Grand Prix was the right decision as it risked compromising his race.

The Mercedes driver made an extra pit stop 16 laps from the end of the race, taking advantage of a late Virtual Safety Car period. It dropped him from second place to third behind his team mate George Russell.
Antonelli was able to repass his team mate for second place after Mercedes ordered Russell to let him through. However Antonelli was unable to gain on race leader Lando Norris.
Afterwards Antonelli said the strategy call had unnecessarily risked both their races, even though he had been struggling on his previous set of tyres.
“It was a difficult second half for me, especially in the last stint on the hards,” he said. “I was just really struggling. I had little confidence in the car and it was not easy.
“Then obviously we pitted [under the VSC] and also that was a bit tricky. But then also George, I have to thank him because he made my life a lot easier.

“But I still think probably we could have stayed out and gone until the end with the same set [of tyres] because it put us a little bit at risk. Also, I feel we put George at risk with having to let me by and everything.”

Although he led most of the race, Antonelli said he was unlikely to win it. “I still think, at the end of the day, it was a great team execution with how things were,” he said. “”I think today [second place] was the maximum we could have done because the pace of the McLarens, especially in the second half, was just too strong.”

“It was a good ending of a difficult weekend for me where I struggled with the feeling of the car, did a lot of mistakes on my side – sprint quali, quali, also in today’s race with Lando I could have defended a bit better,” he added. “So for sure there were things that I didn’t do well this weekend, and for sure the feeling wasn’t as good.”
keyPointsZh: 他在比赛还剩16圈时利用虚拟安全车进站，从第二掉到第三，位于队友拉塞尔之后。
梅赛德斯随后命令拉塞尔让车，安东内利重新回到第二，但未能追近领先的诺里斯。
他认为本可以留在外面用同一套轮胎跑到底，并称自己整个周末对赛车感觉不佳、犯了不少错误。
keyPointsEn: He pitted 16 laps from the end under the Virtual Safety Car, dropping from second to third behind his team mate Russell.
Mercedes then ordered Russell to let him through, and Antonelli regained second but could not close on leader Norris.
He felt they could have stayed out on the same set of tyres to the end, and said he struggled with the car's feeling all weekend and made several mistakes.

items.titleZh: 诺里斯为何说“我没有一辆能争冠的车”？
items.summaryZh: 尽管连续赢下两场大奖赛，诺里斯仍表示自己缺乏争冠所需的赛车，认为迈凯伦MCL40只在高速弯强势，低速弯劣势明显，赛季剩余比赛会很艰难。

media.altZh: 诺里斯为何说“我没有一辆能争冠的车”？

items.originalTitle: 诺里斯为何说“我没有一辆能争冠的车”？
items.summaryEn: Despite winning two consecutive grands prix, Lando Norris insists he lacks the car needed to fight for the championship, saying the McLaren MCL40 is only strong in high-speed corners while its slow-corner weakness makes the rest of the season very tough.
detailZh: 是什么让诺里斯说“我没有一辆能争冠的车”？
尽管连续赢下两场大奖赛，兰多·诺里斯仍坚称，他对在剩余比赛中争夺F1世界冠军没有信心。
我们的专家解读赛车运动中最重要的故事。
2026赛季F1锦标赛正处于一个奇特的交汇点：没有人愿意承认自己拥有最好的赛车。
积分领跑者基米·安东内利在荷兰大奖赛输给兰多·诺里斯获得亚军后表示，梅赛德斯已不再拥有最好的赛车——事实上，它可能只是第三好的。
但诺里斯目前以159分位居第四，安东内利为242分。尽管连续赢下两场大奖赛，他仍决心淡化关于他将在赛季后半段发起反击的说法。“我没有一辆我需要的能争冠的车，”他在荷兰大奖赛获胜后说。
许多读者会忍不住引用所谓的“曼迪·赖斯-戴维斯原则”——“嗯，他们当然会那么说，不是吗？”
不过，明确的是，在最新技术规则下，赛车之间的相对优势仍存在差异，这让竞争格局变得复杂。粗略来说，迈凯伦MCL40在高速弯中如鱼得水，法拉利SF-26在带着良好速度进入低速弯方面很强，而梅赛德斯W17则介于两者之间。这使得竞争平衡在很大程度上取决于赛道布局。
诺里斯的观点是，他的赛车不够全面，无法像去年迈凯伦在大多数赛道上都是标杆那样，在剩余各站中占据统治地位。
诺里斯淡化了荷兰大奖赛胜利的意义。
“我们在某些领域有一辆很强的车，”他说。“不像去年那样我们在所有地方都很好。我们在高速方面非常非常强。我们把车提升最多的地方就是高速性能。”
“在高速方面没人能与我们匹敌。这是好事。我在7号弯、8号弯对梅赛德斯的圈速优势大得离谱。”
“但他们在低速方面对我们的优势也大得离谱。因此我没有信心说，是的，我可以在赛季剩余时间里轻松争冠。我知道我刚连续赢了两场比赛、连续拿了两 个杆位，但目前我没有一辆我需要的能争冠的车。”
“我知道这话分量很重，但我认为去年我明白了赛车需要什么、我需要做什么。我知道自己现在的水平以及我能发挥到什么程度。我也清楚我需要赛车给我什么——以及接下来哪些赛道我们肯定会更挣扎。”
问题比简单地说某辆赛车在某种弯角快更复杂。今年的赛车更短、更窄、也略轻——而且底盘特性与动力单元性能的关联比以往任何时候都更紧密，因为入弯速度会影响能量回收。
迈凯伦选择短轴距，这帮助其在赛季初节省重量，但也固化了某些短板，即车队能从底板榨取多少空气动力学载荷。

Our experts decode the most important stories in motorsport.

Championship leader Kimi Antonelli said after finishing second to Lando Norris in the Dutch Grand Prix that Mercedes no longer has the best car – indeed, that it may only be the third best.

But Norris, now fourth in the standings with 159 points to Antonelli’s 242, was determined to play down talk of him staging a comeback in the final half of the season, despite winning two consecutive grands prix. "I don't have the car I need to fight for a championship," he said after his Dutch GP victory.
Many readers would be tempted to cite the so-called Mandy Rice-Davies principle – "Well they would say that, wouldn’t they?"

What’s clear, though, is that under the latest technical regulations there is still a difference in relative strengths between cars which complicates the competitive picture. In broad-brush terms the McLaren MCL40 thrives in fast corners, Ferrari’s SF-26 is strong in terms of carrying good speed into slow corners, while the Mercedes W17 is somewhere between the two. That makes the competitive balance heavily dependent on circuit layout.
Norris’s contention is that his car is insufficiently rounded to be dominant across the remaining rounds in the way last year’s McLaren was the car to beat at most tracks.
Norris played down the significance of his Dutch GP victory

"We have a strong car in certain areas," he said. "It's not like last year where we were pretty good everywhere. We're very, very strong in high speed. The place we've improved the car the most is high-speed performance.
"No one matches us in high speed. And that's a good thing. My pace advantage to Mercedes in Turn 7, Turn 8 was crazy.

"But their advantage that they have to us in slow speed is also crazy. And therefore I don't have the confidence to say, yeah, I can easily fight for a championship for the rest of the season. I know I've just won two races in a row and two poles in a row, but at the minute I don't have the car I need to fight for a championship.

"And I know that's quite a big comment, but I think last year I understood what is needed from a car and what was needed from me. And I know the level that I am now and what I can perform at. And I know just what I need from the car – and what tracks we have coming up where we're going to certainly struggle more."

The issue is more complex than simply saying a particular car is fast around a certain type of corner. This year’s cars are shorter, narrower and slightly lighter – and the chassis characteristics are more interconnected with power unit performance than ever before, given the influence of corner-entry speeds on energy harvesting.

McLaren's decision to run a short wheelbase, helping it save weight at the start of the season, has baked in certain shortcomings in terms of how much aerodynamic load the team can squeeze from the floor.

Performance is often hugely variable between tyre compounds. In Saturday’s sprint race, running mediums, Norris struggled with rear degradation and was overtaken by Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc in the closing stages. In the grand prix he took the restart on used softs, was passed by Antonelli at the start, and didn’t really get into the race until the hard-compound tyres went on.
Norris was able to pressure championship leader Antonelli later in the Zandvoort race

"We put on the hard tyres," he said. "We were a bit more aggressive with how we wanted to approach the stint. And we turned things around. I had that feeling in the car that I wanted. I went from just not feeling like I was going to win a race to at least we can force him [Antonelli] to make mistakes.

"When I get what I need from a car, when I have the front I want, when I get the confidence with the rear on entries – just when I get what I need to be able to know and predict every single corner, I'm going to win a race."

Norris has a driving style slightly more aligned to Max Verstappen than the likes of George Russell or even his own team-mate, Oscar Piastri. Rather than separating the throttle off/brake on and turning phases, he likes to blend the throttle and brakes and take a shallower approach angle. Essentially he is feeling for the point in the overlap where the front tyres begin to exert more lateral grip, which helps rotate the car and carry more speed into the corner, towards the apex.

This requires the car not only to have a 'strong' front end, but also to communicate what the front tyres are doing, which represents a tough engineering challenge. Modern F1 cars require a consistent ride height for the aerodynamics to function optimally, so the suspension geometry is designed to minimise dive and squat. A side of this is that it saps driver 'feel'.

Some can live with that, some can’t, which is why McLaren designed an alternate front suspension geometry with a revised kingpin angle for Norris when he was floundering at the beginning of last season. Once he has that feel he can be very adaptable in terms of his lines and the degree of overlap between throttle and brake, which is why he thrives in low-grip conditions.
But although he has a huge amount of adaptability within this range, he still needs that strong front end, good transmission of feel, and confidence that the rear axle will rotate predictably on cue.
"It's clear where our weaknesses are," Norris concluded. "Therefore we need to attack those things. And until we do that, it's still going to be a very tough end of the season."

detailZh: 在荷兰大奖赛上F1车手提出批评后，国际汽联解释安全车带队的编队圈
多位F1车手认为，在安全车后方他们无法充分为轮胎升温，以便进行静态起步。国际汽联解释了为何出于安全考虑选择这种做法
由于发车程序期间开始下雨，赞德沃特举行的F1荷兰大奖赛开局阶段陷入混乱。
马克斯·维斯塔潘在比赛第一圈最后一个弯道的出口发生严重撞车。这位红牛车手承认这完全是自己的失误。这位荷兰车手以为自己可以重新踩下油门，但赛道的那个路段显然仍然太湿。
在维斯塔潘身后，加布里埃尔·博托莱托也差点撞车，不过他奇迹般地把奥迪赛车控制住了，没有撞上护墙，而更了不起的是他的队友尼科·霍肯伯格居然避开了他。
这位德国车手立刻通过无线电表示，他担心自己会侧面撞上博托莱托。

The opening stages of the Formula 1 Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort descended into chaos after rain had started to fall during the grid procedure.

Max Verstappen crashed heavily on the exit of the final corner on the opening lap of the race. The Red Bull driver admitted that it was entirely his own mistake. The Dutchman thought he could get back on the throttle, but that part of the track was clearly still too wet.

Behind Verstappen, Gabriel Bortoleto also came close to crashing, although he miraculously managed to keep his Audi out of the wall, while it was even more remarkable that team-mate Nico Hulkenberg managed to avoid him.
The German immediately said over the radio that he feared he was going to T-bone Bortoleto.
"It was just that corner, if I'm very honest with you. It was full wets, that place. I think that's why Max lost it and it was the same for me," Bortoleto said in the media pen post-race.
"I was on the downside of the banking. I did a little reaction move to the left, I think, when I saw big smoke coming up ahead. And when I did that, I just went as well."
According to Gasly, F1 drivers would have been able to get their tyres up to temperature more effectively if the formation lap had been completed without the safety car
Would a normal formation lap have been better?

According to the drivers, the rest of the track had already dried by that point, meaning it was simply a matter of surviving the final two corners. Starting on slicks therefore made sense, as did the FIA’s decision to opt for a standing start.
That said, several drivers were critical of how the start procedure was carried out at Zandvoort.

"If we would go the way we did with one lap behind the safety car and a standing start, then I would have preferred to just do a normal out-lap, so we would have pushed a bit faster,” Pierre Gasly said when asked by Motorsport.com.
"I thought the point was to go at least once through the last corner and the banking with the safety car before doing the normal race start. And yeah, it was damp."
According to the Alpine driver, the FIA would have been better off choosing between two conventional options: a rolling start behind the safety car or a standing start with a normal formation lap.

"I'm sure we'll review at the next race what the drivers' feedback was," Gasly continued. "But I think it was either no safety car and only one formation lap or with the safety car at least giving us one extra lap."
Red Bull stand-in Liam Lawson shared that view and added that he already knew before the start that the procedure would lead to chaos.
Lawson emphasises that he deliberately left more margin than his team-mate Verstappen in the final corner
"I don't know why we had the safety car. To do a standing start and also do a lap behind the safety car makes no sense," Lawson said when asked by Motorsport.com.

"I'm not sure what the reasoning of that was, but I feel like we could all see that coming. We were all probably saying the same thing before when we got the news, but we didn't have control over that."

The race director first sent the medical car out for a reconnaissance lap, something an FIA spokesperson said does not normally happen.

The feedback from the medical car was that there was still standing water at Turns 2 and 3, with Turn 3 – the Hugenholtz corner – also being the first banked corner on the circuit. Based on that information, the FIA considered it safer to complete the formation lap behind the safety car.

The intention at that point was to have a standing start, but by completing the formation lap behind the safety car, race control kept both options open. If the standing water had been deemed too dangerous, it could still have opted for a rolling start.
Williams driver Carlos Sainz, however, felt the latter would not have been a solution and would not have prevented the chaos in the final corner.

"I think, given it was towards the end of the lap, a non-standing start, a rolling start, would have ended up in the same result, because by that time we were all one by one," Sainz said. "So I don't think it would have changed much. It's an unfortunate situation with a lot of water in only one corner."
It therefore came down to the drivers’ own judgement, with Lawson stressing that he deliberately left more margin – considerably more than Verstappen, who was running ahead of him.

"It was just impossible. The whole first half of the lap was dry and then the last few corners were completely soaked. So, it was really easy to do that [what Max has done] when you have this much power on a slick tyre," he said.
"I really lifted out of it because honestly I had no confidence in how much grip we were going to have there and I think Max was probably trying to get closer and make an overtake, and just lost it."

detailZh: 基米·安东内利：梅赛德斯“显然”已不再是F1的最佳车队
这支银箭车队在2026年F1赛季开局时占据统治地位，但在近几场大奖赛中受到了更多挑战
安德烈亚·基米·安东内利、梅赛德斯、刘易斯·汉密尔顿、法拉利、兰多·诺里斯、迈凯伦
F1积分榜领跑者基米·安东内利认为，梅赛德斯“显然”已不再拥有最快的赛车——他在荷兰大奖赛上获得了亚军，仅次于兰多·诺里斯。
这位迈凯伦车手在赞德沃特驾驶经过大幅升级的MCL40从杆位起步实现连胜，使得梅赛德斯六站比赛中仅取得两胜，因为法拉利也拿下了两站。
这与银箭车队2026赛季开局的统治性表现形成鲜明对比——当时他们从杆位起步赢下了前六场大奖赛，直到研发竞赛格局逐渐形成。
“我们现在显然已经不是场上最快的车了，”安东内利表示，“我们大概是第二或第三，至少在今天这场比赛中是这样，而迈凯伦迈出了一大步，尤其是自匈牙利站他们带来大型升级包以来。
但我对车队充满信心。车队一直在为即将到来的下一个升级包全力以赴，他们只是想确保它装上之后能发挥出色。
“所以可以肯定的是，在这场比赛中会更加困难，会充满挑战，但我们已经准备好全力以赴，并把握住每一个机会。
“然后希望接下来轮到我们带来能让我们重新占据一点优势的升级包了。”
安德烈亚·基米·安东内利（安东内利），梅赛德斯；乔治·拉塞尔（拉塞尔），梅赛德斯；兰多·诺里斯（诺里斯），迈凯伦
梅赛德斯此前已经预告将在赛季下半段带来一项“规模可观”的升级，但目前尚未确认升级将在何处首次启用，而车手和车队总冠军的争夺都正在接近高潮。
安东内利以59分的优势领先队友乔治·拉塞尔以及法拉利的刘易斯·汉密尔顿，而梅赛德斯在车队积分榜上则以87分的优势领先排名第二的意大利车队。
拉塞尔表示，尽管经历了“几个艰难的周末”——他在布达佩斯获得第七名，在赞德沃特获得第三名——接下来两周后将在蒙扎进行比赛。
“我认为我们在那里会稍微更有竞争力一些，”这位英国车手补充道，他的队友将因更换引擎而面临发车位处罚。
“不过，我相信法拉利即将迎来引擎升级，而事实是我们真的不知道。但我确实认为这些高轮胎损耗的赛道非常适合迈凯伦，尤其是兰多。”
“在那种条件下他一直都有点专家风范。我们去年也看到了这一点。蒙扎可能稍有不同，但我认为他们现在必须是被击败的头号目标车队。”
detailEn: Mercedes "clearly" not F1's best team anymore - Kimi Antonelli
The Silver Arrows enjoyed a dominant start to the 2026 F1 campaign, but they have been challenged more in recent grands prix
Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Lando Norris, McLaren
Formula 1 championship leader Kimi Antonelli reckons Mercedes “clearly” no longer boasts the fastest car after finishing runner-up to Lando Norris at the Dutch Grand Prix.
The McLaren driver made it consecutive wins from pole at Zandvoort aboard a heavily upgraded MCL40, making it just two victories in six for Mercedes due to Ferrari also claiming a couple.
It marks a far cry from the dominant start the Silver Arrows enjoyed to 2026 by winning the opening six grands prix from pole, before the development race took shape.

“We’re clearly not the fastest car anymore on the grid,” claimed Antonelli. “We’re probably second or third, at least in today’s race, and McLaren has taken a huge step, especially since Hungary, since the big upgrade package they brought.
“But I’m confident with the team. The team has been working super hard on this next package that is coming up and they just want to make sure that it’s going to work out well once we put it on.
“So for sure, in this race, it’s going to be more difficult, it’s going to be challenging, but we’re ready to do our best and to maximise every opportunity.
“And then hopefully it’s going to be our turn to bring the package that’s going to give us a little bit of the upper hand again.”
Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, George Russell, Mercedes, Lando Norris, McLaren

Mercedes had already teased a ‘sizeable’ upgrade in this second half of the campaign with it yet to be confirmed where that will take place, as both the drivers’ and constructors’ title battles near their climax.
Antonelli leads team-mate George Russell and Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton by 59 points, while Mercedes holds an 87-point advantage over the Italian outfit in second.
That’s despite “a challenging couple of weekends” according to Russell, who finished seventh in Budapest and third at Zandvoort ahead of Monza in two weeks’ time.
“I think we will be slightly more competitive there,” added the Briton, whose team-mate will carry a grid penalty for an engine swap.

“However, I believe Ferrari have an engine upgrade incoming and the truth is we just don't know. But I do believe that these high degradation circuits really suit McLaren very well and especially Lando.
“He's always been a bit of specialist in those conditions. We also saw it last year. Monza may be slightly different, but I think they have to be the team to beat right now.”

items.titleZh: 汉密尔顿：法拉利战术失误让我失去第三名
items.summaryZh: 汉密尔顿在荷兰大奖赛后表示，法拉利未及时使用车队指令导致他损失时间，最终仅获第四，错失第三名。他认为这不是运气不佳，并指出梅赛德斯在执行车队指令上更果断。

items.originalTitle: 汉密尔顿：法拉利的战术让我失去第三名，并非运气不佳
items.summaryEn: Lewis Hamilton said after the Dutch Grand Prix that Ferrari's failure to use team orders in time cost him time and a chance to finish third, leaving him fourth. He insisted it was not bad luck and pointed out that Mercedes executes team orders more decisively.
detailZh: 刘易斯·汉密尔顿告诉法拉利，他们在荷兰大奖赛期间未能使用车队指令，导致他失去了获得第三名的机会。
他在比赛中早些时候追上队友查尔斯·勒克莱尔后损失了时间，最终在乔治·拉塞尔之后获得第四名。汉密尔顿多次敦促法拉利告诉勒克莱尔让他通过，但车队却选择等待一圈，然后让领先的法拉利进站。
“我们不要因为可能更好的结果而耽误自己，”汉密尔顿在追上勒克莱尔时对车队说。
在勒克莱尔身后花费一圈后，汉密尔顿警告法拉利“我们只是在损失时间。”当勒克莱尔进站后，汉密尔顿讽刺地说：“太浪费时间了伙计们，干得好。”
汉密尔顿在比赛最后阶段试图超越拉塞尔，但因虚拟安全车出动而受阻。在他获得第四名后，比赛工程师卡洛斯·桑蒂告诉汉密尔顿：“谢谢你刘易斯，和拉塞尔相比有点不走运。”
“我们不是不走运，”汉密尔顿回答，“我们早些时候损失了时间，这让我们失去了第三名。”
汉密尔顿在赛后解释了他的沮丧，指出梅赛德斯在整体有利时毫不犹豫地交换两位车手的顺序。
“我想赢，”汉密尔顿说。“我来这里是为了赢，当你向前看，看到两位梅赛德斯车手，他们得到指令后立刻执行，这很难。
“他们让基米通过，让他继续比赛。我采用了不同的策略，这里情况不同。
“这有点困难，但我们只能接受，我们会在线下解决。现在我回去后，会和他们谈谈。”
更新：勒克莱尔在阻挡汉密尔顿期间未遵守两次进站指令。
detailEn: Lewis Hamilton told Ferrari they cost him a chance to finish third by failing to use team orders during the Dutch Grand Prix.

He finished fourth behind George Russell after losing time earlier in the race when he caught team mate Charles Leclerc. Hamilton repeatedly urged Ferrari to tell Leclerc to let him through, but the team instead to chose wait a lap and then bring the leading Ferrari into the pits.
“Let’s not hold ourselves up from an potentially better result,” Hamilton told the team when he caught Leclerc.
After spending a lap behind Leclerc, Hamilton warned Ferrari “we’re just losing time.” Once Leclerc came in, Hamilton sarcastically remarked: “Big waste of time guys, good job.”

Hamilton’s attempt to pass Russell at the end of the race was thwarted when the Virtual Safety Car was deployed. After he finished fourth race engineer Carlos Santi told Hamilton: “Thank you Lewis, was a bit unlucky with Russell.”
“We weren’t unlucky,” Hamilton replied, “we lost time earlier on and that cost us P3.”
Hamilton explained his frustration after the race, pointing out Mercedes did not hesitate to swap the order of their two drivers when it benefitted them overall.
“I want to win,” said Hamilton. “I’m here to win and it is difficult when you’re looking ahead and you see the two Mercedes drivers, they get the call and it’s done and they execute straight away.
“They let Kimi by and let him get on with the race. I was on a different strategy and it was not the same here.
“That’s a little bit difficult but we just have to take it, we’ll take it off line. When I go back now, I’ll speak to them about it.”
Update: Leclerc failed to obey two orders to pit while he held Hamilton up

items.titleZh: 法拉利车队指令引争议 汉密尔顿不满赞德福特站执行
items.summaryZh: 荷兰大奖赛期间，刘易斯·汉密尔顿因被队友勒克莱尔阻挡而愈发沮丧，并公开批评法拉利的比赛执行，将其与梅赛德斯的策略安排作对比。
items.originalTitle: 梅赛德斯策略对比加剧汉密尔顿对车队指令的不满
items.summaryEn: Lewis Hamilton grew increasingly frustrated with Ferrari's execution at the Dutch Grand Prix, criticising how the team handled race strategy compared to Mercedes' approach.
detailZh: 法拉利对一级方程式车队指令的处理方式，在赞德沃特举行的荷兰大奖赛期间和之后再次成为热议话题，刘易斯·汉密尔顿批评了车队在比赛中的执行，认为与梅赛德斯的应对方式相比有所不足。
汉密尔顿的不满在赞德沃特比赛的第二段（阶段）中爆发，他觉得自己跟在队友夏尔·勒克莱尔身后损失了时间——勒克莱尔用的是稍微旧一些的中性胎，而汉密尔顿用的是硬胎。
当汉密尔顿提出这个问题后，勒克莱尔被召进站（pit），但他第一次没有照做，汉密尔顿变得越来越恼火。等勒克莱尔终于进站让出位置后，他通过无线电说：“真是损失时间的好办法，伙计们，干得好！”
车队领队弗雷德·瓦塞尔并不认为那一刻对汉密尔顿当时的比赛走势起了关键作用，因为当时的考虑是让他留在赛道上直到比赛结束——所以所谓的损失时间本来就无关紧要。
但虚拟安全车让汉密尔顿获得了一次“打折”的进站，这改变了他整场比赛的走向。
在勒克莱尔进站之前，汉密尔顿紧跟在他后面的两圈似乎让他损失了大约1.5到2秒，而在方格旗挥下之后，这段时间损失仍然萦绕在他心头——因为他最终以微弱差距未能超越拉塞尔拿下第三名。
汉密尔顿多次表示，他认为在队友身后被耽误的那一刻正是第三名和第四名之间的差距所在。
他形容这场比赛“对我来说绝对令人沮丧”，并且一边反复强调称赞法拉利的升级，一边多次指出他的老东家梅赛德斯在处理拉塞尔与安东内利换车问题上的表现形成了令人失望的对比。
"这很难，当你看向前方，看到两位梅赛德斯车手——他们接到指令，事情就完成了，立刻执行,"他向F1电视（F1 TV）抱怨道。
"他们让基米（Kimi）过去，让他继续跑比赛。
"而我当时和勒克莱尔（Charles）用的是不同策略——在这里情况并不一样。这有点难接受——但我们会线下处理。等我回去后，我会和他们谈谈这件事。"
与此同时，勒克莱尔也谈不上高兴。
法拉利从未下达过交换位置的指令，但正如上文所提到的，车队确实让他进站，以此作为应对当时局面的替代方案。
勒克莱尔对这一策略并不信服，这也是他在执行指令时犹豫不决的关键因素。在那段赛程（阶段）中他一直跟在拉塞尔身后，对于在拉塞尔进站两圈之后才被召进站感到困惑，认为这与拉开对梅赛德斯车手轮胎差距的逻辑相违背。
虽然他在赛后承认随后的虚拟安全车时机让他运气不佳，但他在赛后仍然对第二次进站提出质疑。
"对我来说，拉开与梅赛德斯的轮胎差距非常重要，这样才能在比赛末段强势追赶。我们没能完全做到这一点，所以我们需要看看原因是什么，"他说。
“我当时非常惊讶，因为我们完全按计划进行时却被要求这么早进站。拉塞尔正在进站，那时候正是我们多跑五到十圈、建立轮胎优势、最后在尾声反超拉塞尔的时机。”
当被问及汉密尔顿的沮丧时，他说：“我的第一段非常出色，我不得不提前进站，试图对前面的车手进行反向进站超越（提前进站），有时候这是车队的一种策略博弈。为此，你必须让自己承担一点风险，尤其是在第一段。刘易斯在第二段非常强势，但事情就是这样。”
“我认为有时候我会感到沮丧，有时候刘易斯会感到沮丧，但事情就是如此。”
勒克莱尔还表示，关于他的进站时机“我认为并没有太多争论”。“起初我被要求进站，然后在那圈快结束时我被要求留在赛道上，我照做了，一圈之后我又被要求进站。”
不过，这与他在F1 TV电台频道上可查到的证据有些相悖。
BB[布莱恩·博齐，比赛工程师]：进站，勒克莱尔，进站。
CL：你说的进站是什么意思？为什么在拉塞尔之后两圈才停？
BB[又一次停顿]：勒克莱尔，我们要你进站。
勒克莱尔完成了一圈，没有进站。
BB：那么，进站，夏尔，进站。将换硬胎。再加两格。
证据表明，勒克莱尔当时有足够的时间——虽然不算充裕——来回应那句“我们要进站”，因此在汉密尔顿被阻挡一事中起到了一定作用。但他也可能听错了那条信息，或者希望得到进一步的确认——一圈之后他没有再多争辩，顺从地进了站。
然而，这一情况可能暴露出的是，法拉利的两位车手对车队当前的总冠军形势持有截然不同的看法。
汉密尔顿对天空体育F1频道说：“我来这里是为了取胜，我真心相信这支车队能够赢得胜利。我们本来赢不下这场比赛——但要想赢得总冠军，你就必须拿下每一个积分。”
他在与文字媒体的见面会上还意味深长地提到了一件他与安东内利共同拥有的东西——那就是在积分榜上担任车队头号车手的地位。
不过，汉密尔顿目前落后安东内利59分，领先勒克莱尔28分，因此目前没有任何迹象表明法拉利会优先考虑汉密尔顿在车手总冠军上的收益而牺牲勒克莱尔的成绩——当然也完全看不到勒克莱尔会以牺牲自己的利益为代价来帮助汉密尔顿的迹象。
detailEn: Ferrari's approach to Formula 1 team orders became a talking point again during and after the Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort, with Lewis Hamilton criticising his team's execution of the race relative to how Mercedes played its cards.

Hamilton's frustration boiled over during the second stint of the Zandvoort race, as he felt he was losing time behind his team-mate Charles Leclerc - who was on marginally older medium tyres versus Hamilton's hards.

Once Hamilton raised the issue, Leclerc was called into the pits, but didn't comply at the first time of asking, and Hamilton grew increasingly exasperated. Once Leclerc did pit out of the way, he radioed: "Great way of losing time, guys, good job!"

Team boss Fred Vasseur did not feel that moment was key to how Hamilton's race was playing out at the time, given the consideration was to keep him out there until the finish - and so the time loss in question would have been immaterial.
But the virtual safety car giving Hamilton a 'discounted' pitstop changed the complexion of his race.

The earlier two laps right behind Leclerc before he pitted appeared to cost Hamilton around 1.5-2s before he pitted, and that time loss was still firmly on his mind after the chequered flag - as he came up just short of picking off George Russell for third place.
Hamilton repeatedly indicated that he felt that moment of delay behind his team-mate was the difference between third and fourth.

He described the race as "definitely frustrating for me" and, while repeatedly making a point of lauding Ferrari's upgrades, repeatedly pointed to his former team Mercedes's handling of the George Russell-Kimi Antonelli swap as a disappointing contrast.
"It is difficult, when you're looking ahead and you see the two Mercedes drivers - they get the call, and it's done, they execute straight away," he vented to F1 TV.
"They let Kimi by and let him get on with the race.
"And I was on a different strategy [to Charles] - and it's not the same here. And that's a little bit difficult - but we'll take it off-line. When I go back now, I'll speak to them about it."
Leclerc, meanwhile, was hardly happy either.
Ferrari never ordered a swap, but it did, as mentioned above, call him into the pits as an alternate solution to the situation.

Leclerc was unconvinced by this strategy, which was the key factor in his dawdling over the order. He had sat behind Russell in that stint, and was perplexed to be called in two laps after Russell's own pitstop, believing it ran counter to the logic of building a tyre offset to the Mercedes driver.
While he acknowledged after the race that he got unlucky with the subsequent virtual safety car timing, he continued to question that second pitstop after the race.
"For me, it was very important to create a tyre delta to the Mercedes in order to come back strong at the end. We didn't quite do that, so we need to look at why," he said.

"I was very surprised to box so early when we had done exactly what we wanted. George was pitting and so that was the time for us to do five, 10 laps longer to build a tyre delta and to come back at the end on George."

When quizzed about Hamilton's frustrations, he said: "I had a very good first stint, I had to stop early to try and undercut the guys in front and that's a bit of a team game sometimes. You've got to put yourself a little bit at risk, especially in the first stint, for that. Lewis was very strong in the second stint, but it's the way it goes.
"I think sometimes I'll be frustrated, sometimes Lewis will be frustrated, but it's the way it is."

Leclerc also said "I don't think there was much debate" over his pit timing. "At first I was asked to stop and then towards the end of the lap I was asked to stay on track, which I did, and the lap later I was asked to stop."
This, though, runs somewhat counter to the available evidence from his radio channel on F1 TV.
BB [Bryan Bozzi, race engineer]: Box, Charles, box.
CL: What do you mean box-box? Why stop two laps after Russell?
BB [another pause]: Charles, we want to box.
Leclerc finishes the lap without pitting
BB: So, box, Charles, box. Will be for hard. Plus two clicks.

The evidence is that Leclerc had enough time - though not a huge amount - to respond to that "we want to box" and thus played his role in Hamilton being held up. But he could've perhaps misheard that message or hoped for further clarification - and he acquiesced a lap later without further debate.
What the situation has potentially exposed, however, is a different view altogether on Ferrari's current championship situation between its two drivers.
"I'm here to win and I really believe that this team can win. We couldn't win this race - but to win championships you have to pick up every point," Hamilton told Sky F1.
He also made a very pointed reference in his session with the written media to something he shares with Antonelli - the status of being the team's leading driver in the points standings.

But with Hamilton 59 points down on Antonelli and 28 up on Leclerc, there is currently no indication of Ferrari prioritising Hamilton's drivers' championship yield over Leclerc's - and certainly no sign of Leclerc trying to lend a helping hand at his own expense.
keyPointsZh: 汉密尔顿当时使用硬胎，勒克莱尔使用略旧的中性胎，汉密尔顿认为自己被挡而损失时间。
车队随后召勒克莱尔进站，但他第一次并未立即执行，之后让出位置时汉密尔顿在无线电中说：“损失时间的好办法，伙计们，干得漂亮！”
车队领队瓦塞尔认为这一时刻对汉密尔顿的比赛结果并非关键，因为当时的计划是让汉密尔顿留在场上直到比赛结束。
keyPointsEn: Hamilton was on hard tyres while Leclerc ran marginally older mediums, and Hamilton felt he was losing time stuck behind his team-mate.
Leclerc did not pit at the first call, and when he eventually moved aside, Hamilton radioed: "Great way of losing time, guys, good job!"
Team boss Fred Vasseur did not consider the moment decisive, as the plan was to keep Hamilton out until the finish, making the time loss immaterial.

detailZh: 弗兰科·科拉平托和美客多高管在荷兰大奖赛处罚后抨击国际汽联干事
弗兰科·科拉平托在荷兰大奖赛期间被处以两次处罚，这引发了这位阿根廷车手和美客多一位高管的强烈反应，该公司是他在一级方程式的主要赞助商
弗兰科·科拉平托发现自己卷入了国际汽联干事的一场争议的中心，他因在一级方程式荷兰大奖赛发车时在黄旗下违规而受到处罚。
这位阿尔派车手当时正在超越角田裕毅，就在几米之外维斯塔潘发生撞车，触发了黄旗，随后比赛被红旗终止。
科拉平托无法避免完成对角田裕毅的超越，这促使干事展开调查并对他处以通过维修区处罚。这实际上终结了他得分的机会，此前他在比赛早段已经进入前十。阿尔维德·林德布拉德也因对皮埃尔·加斯利的类似动作被处以同样的处罚。
这位阿根廷车手在赛后接受Motorsport.赛车运动网站采访时被问及这一决定时明显感到不满：“正是那次通过维修区处罚毁掉了我们的整场比赛。我的起步非常出色，当时我处于得分区间。是的，就是很棘手，我觉得。
“在这种条件下很难判断，当你在第一圈进行缠斗、做出动作时，赛道又湿又潮，而且是在倾斜弯道上，还有赛车碎片四处飞散。我在完成超越时才看到非常、非常晚才出示的黄旗，而在直道中间、在倾斜弯道上、在湿地条件下，当时大家都在打滑，突然刹车再加速显然危险得多。所以这是一个非常棘手的情况。
“我觉得尽管规则是白纸黑字写明的，但它们应该更加灵活，应该有相应的标准去理解什么更安全或稍微不那么安全。如果有人在赛道的同一段比你慢30公里每小时，你正在超越他，这时黄旗出现了，你其实没什么办法。对这种情况做出反应非常棘手。”
当Motorsport.com问及裁判是否应该更宽容一些、把当时的情况考虑进去时，这位23岁的车手回答道：“我觉得他们的处罚极其严厉。我是说，这是他们的工作，但他们也有责任灵活一点，去理解当时的实际情况。”
“我认为尤其是要分清哪种情况比另一种更危险，当时抓地力那么低，赛道条件又是那样。对我来说，这处罚就是有点太重了。我觉得对我们俩都是如此，对我和小林德布拉德（Lindblad）都是，尤其是那个穿过维修区（drive-through）的处罚，这直接毁了你的整场比赛。感觉太过了，但事情就是这样。”
在比赛后段，科拉平托（Colapinto）又收到了第二次处罚，这次是在黄旗期间再次违规，被罚10秒。裁判还在他的驾照上增加了3个罚分，使他的总罚分达到4分。
自由市场（Mercado Libre）高管猛烈抨击国际汽联（FIA）的裁判
科拉平托并不是唯一批评干事的人。比赛结束后，支持这位阿尔卑斯车手F1职业生涯的阿根廷公司美客多（Mercado Libre）的首席营销官肖恩·萨默斯在X上发帖，对赞德沃特发生的事件表达了不满。
这位公司高管在帖文中@了国际汽联的官方X账号，并写道：“干事们正在扼杀F1的诚信。本赛季他们的表现糟糕透顶，并且影响了比赛结果。是无能？还是不诚实？还是两者皆有？那个组织的文化一定出了严重的问题。”
当这位阿根廷车手在2024年意大利大奖赛开始为威廉姆斯出战时，美客多成为了他的赞助商，并在他转投阿尔卑斯后继续支持他，成为这位车手在F1中的主要支持者之一。
科拉平托最终在周日的比赛中以第14名完赛，他驾驶的是一辆旧版本的阿尔卑斯赛车，因为车队将最新的A526升级件安装在了加斯利的赛车上。
周一，一位阿尔派（阿尔派）发言人发表声明，以澄清其在上文言论之后的立场。
声明中写道：“作为一支车队，我们与这项运动的管理机构密切合作，制定赛道上的行为规则，以确保比赛公平、精彩，并且最重要的是保障安全。在规则的执行以及比赛进行中体育处罚的适用方面，我们完全信任国际汽联（FIA）和赛事干事。”
“我们认为，荷兰大奖赛开局圈因黄旗违规而施加的处罚确实严厉，但我们也承认，依照法律的字面规定，这些处罚是恰当的，并且对所有车手一视同仁地执行，这是我们可以作为车队进行回顾并从中学习的事情。”
detailEn: Franco Colapinto and Mercado Libre executive hit out at FIA stewards after Dutch GP penalties

Franco Colapinto was handed two penalties during the Dutch Grand Prix, prompting a strong reaction from both the Argentine driver and a senior Mercado Libre executive, whose company is his main sponsor in Formula 1
Franco Colapinto found himself at the centre of an FIA stewards’ controversy after being penalised for an infringement under yellow flags at the start of the Formula 1 Dutch Grand Prix.
The Alpine driver was in the process of overtaking Yuki Tsunoda when Max Verstappen crashed a few metres ahead, triggering yellow flags before the race was subsequently stopped by a red flag.

Colapinto was unable to avoid completing the pass on Tsunoda, prompting the stewards to investigate and hand him a drive-through penalty. That effectively ended his hopes of scoring points after he had moved into the top 10 early in the race. Arvid Lindblad was handed the same penalty for a similar move on Pierre Gasly.

The Argentine was visibly unhappy with the decision when asked about it by Motorsport.com after the race: "It was the drive-through that compromised the whole of our race. I made a very good start and I was up there in the points. Yeah, just tricky, I think.

"Tricky to judge in those conditions when you're fighting on lap one, making a move and it's all wet and damp and on the banking, and there are parts of the car flying around. I saw a very, very late yellow flag when I was finishing my overtake, and it was clearly much more dangerous to slam on the brakes and accelerate in the middle of the straight, on the banking and on the wet, when everyone was spinning. So it's a very tricky one.

"I feel that even though the rules are written, they should be much more flexible and they should have the criteria to also understand what's safer or a bit more unsafe. If someone is going 30km/h slower in the same part of the track, you're overtaking them and a yellow flag comes in, there's not a lot you can do. It's very tricky to react to that."

When asked by Motorsport.com whether the stewards should have been more lenient and taken the circumstances into account, the 23-year-old answered: "I feel they have been extremely harsh. I mean, it's their job, but it's also their job to be a bit flexible and understand the situation.

"I think especially what is more dangerous than the other, when the grip is so low and the conditions are like that. To me, it's just a bit harsh. I think for both, for me and Lindblad, but especially a drive-through, it kills your race. It feels too much, but it is what it is."

Later in the race, Colapinto received a second penalty, this time a 10-second penalty, for another infringement during a yellow-flag period. The stewards also added three penalty points to his licence, taking his total to four.
Mercado Libre executive hits out at FIA stewards

Colapinto wasn’t alone in his criticism of the stewards. Following the race, Sean Summers, Mercado Libre's Chief Marketing Officer, the Argentine company that supports the Alpine driver’s career in F1, expressed his frustration with the events at Zandvoort in a post on X.

The company executive tagged the FIA's official X account and wrote: "The Stewards are killing the integrity of F1. This season they are proving to be horrible and impacting race results. Incompetence? Dishonesty? Both? Something is seriously broken in that organisation's culture."

Mercado Libre became a sponsor of Colapinto when the Argentine began racing for Williams at the 2024 Italian Grand Prix and continued to support him following his move to Alpine, becoming one of the driver's main backers in F1.
Colapinto ultimately finished 14th on Sunday, driving an older version of Alpine's car after the team fitted its latest A526 upgrades to Gasly's car.
On Monday, an Alpine spokesperson issued a statement to clarified its stance following the above comments.

“As a team, we work closely with the sport’s governing body on the rules of engagement on track to ensure fair and exciting racing and, most importantly, safety,” the statement read. “We fully trust the FIA and the Stewards when it comes to the policing of these rules and the application of sporting penalties during a live race scenario.

“We believe the penalties applied for Yellow Flag Infringements during the opening laps of the Dutch Grand Prix were indeed harsh, but acknowledge they fit the punishment based on the letter of the law and were consistently applied across all competitors and is something we can review and learn from as a team.”
